newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati says will not vote in poll.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati says will not vote in poll.

text.p: Ousted minority Indonesian party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri said on Thursday she would not vote in next week's general elections, and told her supporters they should also not vote for the party she previously led.
"With very deep concern, I declare today that I will not use my political right as a citizen (to vote) in this election," she told about 500 chanting supporters at her south Jakarta home.

Megawati, eldest daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, was ousted by a government-backed faction as leader as the Christian-nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) in June last year.
She has declared the takeover of the party illegal and unconstitutional and has challenged it in the courts, so far without success.

"What is described as the PDI, it is the result of the Medan Congress (when she was ousted last June). It is illegal and unconstitutional, therefore to vote for it on May 29, 1997, is also illegal and unconstitutional," she said.

The government-recognised wing of the PDI, the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and the ruling Golkar are the only parties legally entitled to contest the five-yearly local and national elections next Thursday.
